collector_failure: WinRM transport interruption after the trial during two KD assertion prompts
findings: The first complete failed DWM draw has a 24x24 BGRA target, 72 nonindexed vertices forming 24 triangles, and a [2,0,24,18] scissor. Its color and alpha blend factors are ZERO and INV_SRC_ALPHA with ADD. The current renderer supports destination-in but rejects this inverse mask before dispatch; offline CPU replay reproduces rejection.
DWM records 70 completed draws and 5 successful Present callbacks. The physical NPU worker returns 71 successful DWM packets. Receipt, callback and delivered-frame counts are separate observations.

Two opaque-black frames reach the collector and software viewer. One arrives while the collector sole-display gate is true. The harness sends Shift once on sole entry and never attempts Start because no visible desktop content arrives.

After the first failure, DWM also records vertex-buffer binding rejections and captures a 200-word pixel shader containing derivative opcodes 11 and 12, which the parser does not support. The next build adds targeted binding diagnostics; these later failures do not yet establish which path a successful primary device would take.

The package was initially generated with an incorrectly transcribed source revision. That uninstalled package is preserved as driver-package-v86-metadata-rejected. A fresh package using git rev-parse HEAD was built, verified, and is the only v86 package transferred to the guest.

The collector later exits with a WinRM transport failure while the debugger is awaiting two DWM assertion responses. This occurs after both devices are removed; frame and sole-gate observations above remain bounded to their timestamps. The raw stderr and subsequent recovery are retained.
Both custom devices and transport configuration are removed. No usable desktop, physical scanout offload or Tahoma benefit is established.
